evidence: gpt-oss-120b: "candidates are vertices that can still be chosen" and "cur_set is current independent set (bitmask)"
affordance_in_statement: A NAND gate outputs a HIGH signal unless both of its input pins are driven HIGH... every single one of the m NAND gates must output a HIGH signal... drive exactly k of the input pins HIGH
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: the NAND requirements are intrinsically equivalent to selecting an independent set of size k. They could only be re-presented indirectly as a generic pairwise-compatibility constraint, which would obscure but not remove the structure.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognized the problem as finding an independent set of exactly k vertices and represented candidate sets with bitmasks.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A gate is HIGH unless both endpoints are selected HIGH, so no wired pair may occur together in the selected set.

common_affordance: The direct reduction from satisfying all NAND gates to selecting an independent set of exactly k vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The meet-in-the-middle independent-set implementation terminated with a runtime error.
It tried every k-subset using itertools.combinations, which is exponential and timed out.
It enumerated all 2^n masks and checked every selected pair, which timed out.

recommended_edit: No single wording edit can defeat the surviving approach without changing the underlying task; the independent-set structure is the core problem rather than an incidental affordance.
regression_risk: Any merely cosmetic rewording could still be parsed back into the same independent-set problem and would not reliably affect the survivor.
